text:
(4) Where material consists of information which has not been recorded the prosecutor
discloses it for the purposes of this section by securing that it is recorded in such form
as he thinks fit and—
(a) by securing that a copy is made of it and that the copy is given to the accused,
or
(b) if in the prosecutor’s opinion that is not practicable or not desirable, by
allowing the accused to inspect it at a reasonable time and a reasonable place
or by taking steps to secure that he is allowed to do so.
Criminal Procedure and Investigations Act 1996 (c. 25)
